label: GO step: choosing a1 right after a rewarded (common or first-in-window) trial, early/mid episode
explanation: Fires only at GO steps (never at D1 or D2) when the previous trial was rewarded and the agent is about to choose a1 (model_act==1: 99.5% of mass; with upcoming action==1 instead the result is nearly the same). It is silent after unrewarded trials, almost silent when choosing a2 (0.8% of mass) and after rare-transition trials (1%). It also depends strongly on position in the episode: it fires mostly in trials 10-69, sparsely in 70-79, and never from trial 80 on, which suggests a slow drift in hidden state rather than a task variable. Predicate (no future variables; model_act is the agent own computed choice): dev P 0.54, R 0.95, F1 0.69, mass recall 0.99. Precision is incomplete: many rewarded a1 GO steps stay below threshold. In example windows the magnitude ramps up across consecutive rewarded a1 trials (e.g. 0 -> 0.5 -> 0.66 -> 0.71) and is largest when the policy logit for a1 and the value are high (71% of mass where choice > 8.07). Adding value or good-state conditions did not improve F1. In effect it is a reward-driven stay-on-a1 signal at the choice step.
